data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002 grounds its mechanism in a bird-flock 'leader bird' analogy, but its own disanalogy note concedes flock synchrony arises from real-time sensory feedback and local interaction, whereas the target's actual cause is identical offline-trained models. The 'leader bird' is a real-time, locally-coupled signal, not an identical offline artifact; thus the analogy supplies no causal bridge for how shared training data synchronizes independent operators' failure timing. The transfer claim that 'any decentralized system with a hidden shared signal will exhibit correlated failures' is an unsupported leap: it substitutes a shared static artifact for a real-time coordination signal without a mechanism connecting model identity to correlated failure events.
